scenes.visual: Title: Pain Genes and Pain Relief. Show SCN9A beside a Nav1.7 channel, then two branches labelled pain loss and pain syndromes. No concentration curve.

scenes.tts: Inherited changes in one sodium channel gene can remove pain or cause severe pain syndromes. That is strong causal evidence for a channel in human pain, and a reason to target it with drugs. Three families in northern Pakistan had members who had never experienced pain. They had two broken copies of S C N nine A, the gene for N A V one point seven. In cultured cells, their mutant channels passed no current above background.

scenes.visual: Lead with SCN9A branching into pain loss and severe pain syndromes. Then show three family pedigree chips, two broken SCN9A copies, and mutant Nav1.7 recordings at background. Label the recording as mutant human channels expressed in cultured cells. Connect the genetic evidence to a drug-target symbol.

scenes.tts: Other variants in the same gene cause pain syndromes. Some channels open at more negative voltages and close more slowly. Others fail to inactivate properly, leaving persistent sodium current. Same gene, different channel defects, different pain phenotypes.

scenes.visual: Extend the SCN9A comparison. Label primary erythermalgia: activation shifts negative and deactivation slows. Label paroxysmal extreme pain disorder: impaired fast inactivation and persistent current. Use qualitative channel-state sketches, without invented voltages or current values.

scenes.tts: Nociceptor spikes draw on N A V one point seven, one point eight, and one point nine. The first two contribute to the spike. One point nine mainly sets resting potential and subthreshold excitability. More channel function need not mean more firing. Some human one point nine variants depolarized rat sensory neurons enough to impair spike generation.

scenes.visual: Show the three channel subtypes in a nociceptor membrane. Associate Nav1.7 and Nav1.8 with a schematic spike and Nav1.9 with resting potential and subthreshold excitability; do not imply exclusive roles. In a separate panel explicitly labelled human Nav1.9 variants expressed in rat sensory neurons, show sustained depolarization reducing availability of other sodium channels and impairing spikes. No numeric axes.

scenes.tts: The drug story went differently. A selective N A V one point seven blocker did not significantly beat placebo in a trial of painful diabetic neuropathy. Suzetrigine blocks N A V one point eight. It reduced pain after surgery versus placebo in both phase three trials. These were different pain conditions, not a direct comparison of targets. Neither surgery trial demonstrated superiority over hydrocodone with acetaminophen. Approval in the United States followed in January twenty twenty five for moderate to severe acute pain in adults.

Neither surgery trial demonstrated superiority over hydrocodone with acetaminophen. Approval in the United States followed in January 2025 for moderate-to-severe acute pain in adults.

scenes.visual: Use separate trial cards: PF-05089771, painful diabetic neuropathy, no significant improvement versus placebo; suzetrigine, Nav1.8, postoperative pain, benefit versus placebo in both phase 3 trials. Emphasize demonstrated postoperative pain relief. Add no superiority over hydrocodone/acetaminophen and a January 2025 US approval card with the adult acute-pain indication. Do not depict target-to-target comparison or opioid equivalence.

scenes.tts: The neurons themselves are diverse. A molecular label, a conduction class, and a functional state describe different things. A label does not fix a stimulus function. Nociceptors can change state through sensitization. In cultured mouse sensory neurons, nerve growth factor brought out mechanical currents that required PIEZO two.

scenes.visual: Show three intersecting axes: molecular label, conduction class, functional state. Then show separate soma-indentation conditions in cultured mouse CHRNA3-positive sensory neurons: nearly no mechanical current before NGF, induced current after NGF, and prevention of that induced current with PIEZO2 knockdown. Label these as cultured somata, not intact endings. Do not show repeated recordings of one tracked cell.

scenes.tts: One smaller point closes the story. In dissociated adult human sensory neurons, suzetrigine generally reduced repetitive firing without eliminating it. Blocking a channel is not neuronal silence. The clinical trials measured pain relief.

scenes.visual: Label this panel smaller point: one human-neuron recording study. Show qualitative before-and-after spike trains, reduced but still present after suzetrigine, explicitly labelled schematic and dissociated adult human sensory neurons. End on three distinct evidence cards: inherited variants, neuronal recordings, clinical pain relief. No fitted curve or residual-current calculation.
End card: Pain Genes and Pain Relief. Retain SCN9A pain-loss/pain-syndrome branches and the separate Nav1.8 postoperative pain-relief card.
